name: Water resources planning guideline - detail
fact: Updated 16 June 2026; WRMPs must be prepared at least every five years, reviewed annually, and normally cover at least 25 years of supply-demand planning.
gate: Strategic WRMP evidence does not prove site-level water connection capacity or a development-specific supply commitment.

name: Water resources planning guideline - landing
fact: Environment Agency, Natural Resources Wales and Ofwat jointly publish the current WRMP guidance; the page records the 16 June 2026 update.
gate: Guidance discovery is not parcel evidence.

name: Managing water abstraction
fact: Updated 8 April 2026; explains how river-basin plans, CAMS, water-company plans and national frameworks are combined to manage abstraction and future water needs.
gate: Catchment policy does not establish a specific development's supply headroom.

name: Water demand Environment Act target delivery plan
fact: Updated 16 July 2026; England's statutory target is a 20% reduction in public-water-supply use per head by 2038 from the 2019-20 baseline, with interim targets.
gate: National demand targets are contextual and cannot be converted directly into parcel-level water availability.

name: Water resources planning guideline consultation outcome
fact: Updated 8 May 2026; the Environment Agency confirmed the consultation outcome and publication of updated WRMP guidance.
gate: Consultation outcome is process evidence, not site capacity.

name: Environment Agency business plans collection
fact: Updated 17 July 2026; the collection includes the Environment Agency business plan for 2026-27.
gate: Corporate priorities are context only.

name: Environment Agency business plan 2026-27
fact: Updated 17 July 2026; EA says it will work with the Water Delivery Taskforce so water supply and wastewater treatment support a healthy environment and economy.
gate: Programme-level commitments do not create a site-specific capacity approval.

name: EA review of revised draft regional and WRMPs
fact: EA's review covers revised regional and company water-resource plans and highlights where action and improvement are required for secure supplies to 2050.
gate: The review is regional/company-level and must be reconciled with each current final WRMP.

name: Water resources 2024-25 annual performance analysis
fact: EA states 2025-26 is the first PR24/WRMP24 delivery year for most companies and expects progress on WRMP24 schemes.
gate: Annual performance evidence is company/programme level, not a connection offer.

name: Ofwat water resource planning
fact: Ofwat states WRMPs are statutory five-year plans covering at least the next 25 years and addressing population growth, climate change and abstraction pressures.
gate: Regulatory planning context does not equal local network headroom.

name: Thames Water WRMP24
fact: Thames Water says government-approved WRMP24 was published in October 2024 and plans supply-demand balance out to 2075.
gate: WRMP options and deficits are strategic; exact development capacity requires local network/connection evidence.

name: Thames Water WRMP24 publication news
fact: Thames Water states its WRMP24 forecasts about 1 billion additional litres per day may be needed by 2050 and proposes major supply and demand measures.
gate: Forecast need is not a parcel supply commitment.

name: Thames Water government approval news
fact: Thames Water records government approval of WRMP24 and major strategic options including reservoir and recycling projects.
gate: Approval of a company plan does not approve individual development connections.

name: Anglian Water WRMP24
fact: Anglian Water publishes WRMP24 reports, data tables and zone material and notes an April 2025 revision aligned to PR24 baseline out-turns.
gate: Use current zone-specific tables; company plan alone cannot establish parcel capacity.

name: Anglian Water resource-zone summaries
fact: Anglian Water publishes WRMP24 summaries for seven planning areas including Lincs/Notts, Ruthamford, Fenland, Norfolk, East Suffolk/Essex, Cambs/West Suffolk and Hartlepool.
gate: Zone-level evidence is closer to location but still not a development connection confirmation.

name: Anglian Water drought plan
fact: Anglian Water's drought-plan page links the current WRMP24 and explains climate, environment and population-growth pressures on supplies.
gate: Drought-plan measures are resilience context, not normal-development capacity.

name: Severn Trent WRMP24 final documents
fact: Severn Trent publishes final WRMP24 documents and downloadable planning data tables.
gate: Use resource-zone tables and current operational evidence before any site capacity conclusion.

name: Southern Water WRMP
fact: Southern Water publishes its final-draft WRMP24 and supporting technical material after consultation and regulatory revision.
gate: Final-draft/company-plan status is strategic and does not confirm site-level supply.

name: Southern Water long-term water-supply plan update
fact: Southern Water says its final draft WRMP24 was published 30 May 2025 and includes leakage, efficiency, recycling, reservoir and transfer options.
gate: Strategic projects are not development connection offers.

name: Southern Water WRMP introduction
fact: Southern Water states its WRMP24 covers 2025-2075 and is coordinated with the Water Resources South East group.
gate: Fifty-year planning scope is context only.

name: Yorkshire Water WRMP24
fact: Yorkshire Water says Defra granted permission to publish its final WRMP24 and provides technical documents and planning tables.
gate: Published WRMP evidence does not substitute for a local connection/capacity response.

name: Portsmouth Water resources planning
fact: Portsmouth Water publishes final technical/non-technical WRMP24 documents and detailed appendices.
gate: Strategic plan does not prove parcel capacity.

name: South Staffs Water WRMP24 publications
fact: South Staffs Water's publication index exposes final WRMP24, appendices, customer summary and 2024-25 annual review.
gate: Index evidence must be tied to the current WRMP document and exact supply area.

name: South West Water WRMP
fact: South West Water publishes WRMP24 plan material, technical reports, appendices and data tables.
gate: Plan material is strategic and may include draft/revised stages; current final status must be checked before site use.

name: Wessex Water WRMP24
fact: Wessex Water says it received direction to publish its final WRMP24 in September 2024 and plans long-term water security.
gate: Company plan is not parcel-level supply confirmation.

name: Wessex Water environmental information library
fact: Updated 20 January 2026; the library includes WRMP24 main plan, zone-boundary files, demand/supply forecasts and environmental assessments.
gate: Zone boundaries and reports require exact spatial matching; no connection is inferred.

name: SES Water WRMP
fact: SES Water publishes WRMP24 for 2025-2075 with headroom, demand, deployable-output and environmental appendices.
gate: Use exact zone/headroom evidence; plan publication alone is not a supply offer.

name: SES Water WRMP summary booklet
fact: SES Water's official summary describes its 50-year plan for 2025-2075.
gate: Summary-level evidence cannot support parcel-level headroom.
